Idea

Demand to shipment

The shape of the whole chain, in one screen. Six module lanes, six stages, master data to a confirmed shipment. Ten minutes, and it is the first thing to read: every process is one route across it.

Level 2 is the detail. The session map starts at sales demand and names every session with its route and action. This page is the shape.

The branch that is the whole point

Two orders for the same item can take completely different routes, and the difference is decided before anything is created. If on-hand plus on-order already covers the demand, order planning generates nothing and the sales order goes straight to release and shipping — stages 3, 4 and 5 never happen. If it does not, MRP proposes, the transfer makes those proposals real, and Procurement and Manufacturing supply what is missing.

That branch is the edge marked SKIPS 3, 4, 5 in section 5, and it is domain rather than drawing: which stages a route bypasses is a fact about Infor LN, and where the line is drawn on the page is not.

    Stage Prepare

    What changes in it The master data the rest of the chain reads

    2

    Stage Demand

    What changes in it A sales order exists, and the branch is decided

    3

    Stage Plan

    What changes in it MRP nets and explodes; proposals appear

    4

    Stage Transfer

    What changes in it The boundary. Proposals become real orders. Planning ends here

    5

    Stage Execute

    What changes in it Components received and the item built

    6

    Stage Deliver

    What changes in it The sales order released, advised, picked, frozen and confirmed

  • A number is a position on the walk. The thirteen numbered tiles are what a reader passes through in order — the steps they take, the checkpoints the route turns on, and the shipment that ends it — numbered in the order they are walked rather than the order the lanes are printed, so 8 · Warehouse Receipt comes before 9 · Production Orders because the components have to be on hand before the order can consume them.

    Thirteen tiles carry no number, for four different reasons. Four are setup: what must already be true before the walk starts, and they reach the walk by feed rather than by flow. Three are results the system produced on its own — the two proposals MRP wrote, and the finished item in stock. Two are lookups, and a lookup carries no edge at all: it is a detour taken for information, and the walk is the same whether or not you take it. Four are checkpoints where a route turns because something is short. They are placeholders: each names what has not been walked, and a walk completes it.

    Master Data

    items · Items and groups tcibd0501m100 · stage 1 · step

    • Route — no menu entry; tick a row in Items tcibd0501m000, Master Data➔Items➔Items, and drill in
    • Does — hold the item every other lane reads
    • Do - confirm the item exists with its group, defaults and unit
    • Opens — Create test items · Create the three items

    buyfrom · Item - Purchase tdipu0601m000 · stage 1 · step

    • Route — no menu entry; Go to Details from Items - Purchase tdipu0101m000, Procurement➔Master Data➔Items➔Items - Purchase
    • Does — carry the buy-from partner a purchased item needs
    • Do - check the Item - Business Partner tab has a row. Without one the transfer refuses to create a purchase order at all

    bom · Bill of material and routing · stage 1 · outcome

    • Does — define what a made item is built from and how, both Approved
    • Opens — Create test items · Build the job shop bill of material, Build the job shop routing
    • Check — Production and planning section 2

    cluster · Planning cluster row on the item · stage 1 · outcome

    • Does — make the item visible to order planning. Without it the item is absent from the plan rather than refused
    • Opens — Run order planning · Make the item visible to planning

    Sales

    1 · Sales Order Intake Workbench tdsls4601m200 · stage 2 · step

    • Route — Sales➔Orders➔Order Intake Workbench
    • Does — create the demand the rest of the chain answers
    • Do - enter the order and approve it
    • Opens — Ship from stock · Create and approve the sales order; Run order planning · Create demand; Plan to shipment · Create the demand

    2 · Does on-hand cover it? · stage 2 · decision

    • Does — decide the whole route. On-hand plus on-order against the demand, and nothing announces the answer
    • Read — Inventory 360 whwmd4300m000, Warehousing➔Inventory 360
    • Check — Planning foundations section 7

    allocated · Stock promised to other orders · stage 2 · gate

    • Does — decide silently how much of on-hand is free for this order, which is the available-to-promise check. The figure decision 2 really tests is projected inventory, time-phased, not the on-hand total — Item Order Plan §2.1. Not documented for this release.
    • Read — Item Order Plan cprrp0520m000, Planning➔Order Planning➔Item Order Plan
    • Setting — CTP Horizon in Items - Planning cprpd1100m000, Planning➔Master Data➔Items➔Items - Planning

    10 · Release Sales Order Lines to Warehousing tdsls4501m140 · stage 6 · step

    • Route — no menu entry; the Release to Warehousing tab of Sales Order tdsls4100m900, opened from Sales Order Intake Workbench tdsls4601m200, Sales➔Orders➔Order Intake Workbench
    • Does — hand the approved lines to Warehousing, which creates a warehousing order carrying the sales order number
    • Do - Actions ➔ Release ➔ Release to Warehousing…, set Upto Release Date on or after the line's release date, then RELEASE
    • Opens — Ship from stock · Release to warehousing; Plan to shipment · Ship

    Enterprise Planning

    3 · Planning data exists · stage 3 · gate

    • Does — decide silently whether planning can see the item and every component beneath it
    • Read — Items - Planning cprpd1100m000, Planning➔Master Data➔Items➔Items - Planning
    • Setting — the Clusters tab of Item tcibd0501m100, no menu entry; tick a row in Items tcibd0501m000, Master Data➔Items➔Items, and drill in
    • Opens — Run order planning · Make the item visible to planning
    • Check — Planning foundations section 3

    4 · Inside the order horizon · stage 3 · gate

    • Does — decide silently whether the delivery date is near enough to plan. Counted in workdays
    • Read — Item Order Plan cprrp0520m000, Planning➔Order Planning➔Item Order Plan
    • Setting — Order Horizon in Items - Planning cprpd1100m000, Planning➔Master Data➔Items➔Items - Planning
    • Opens — Run order planning · Put the demand inside the horizon

    — · Item Order Plan cprrp0520m000 · stage 3 · read

    • Route — Planning➔Order Planning➔Item Order Plan
    • Does — show what planning holds for one item: demand and forecast against scheduled receipts and planned supply. The two gates beside it are conditions LN evaluates and mostly never announces; this is the screen where a reader sees what they decided
    • Do - read the item's plan before the run and again after it, and compare
    • Leaves — nothing. It is a detour for information and the walk is the same whether or not you take it
    • Check — Planning foundations sections 1, 2

    5 · Generate Order Planning (Item) cprrp1220m000 · stage 3 · step

    • Route — no menu entry; reached by drilling in. Not documented for this release.
    • Does — net demand against stock and explode the bill of material
    • Do - run it with Include Child Items
    • Opens — Run order planning · Run MRP, Review the result, Read the pegging tree; Plan to shipment · Run MRP
    • Check — Planning foundations sections 4, 5

    planned-prod · Planned production order · stage 3 · planned

    • Does — propose making the shortfall. Real to nothing outside planning

    planned-purch · Planned purchase order · stage 3 · planned

    • Does — propose buying the shortfall. Real to nothing outside planning

    6 · Transfer Order Planning cppat1210m000 · stage 4 · transfer

    • Route — Planning➔Plan Transfer➔Transfer Order Planning
    • Does — translate a proposal into a real order in its owning module. Planning ends here
    • Do - confirm the planned orders first, then run it once per supply source
    • Setting — Default Supply Source in Items by Site tcibd1550m000, Master Data➔Items➔Items by Site
    • Opens — Plan to shipment · Cross the boundary
    • Check — Planning foundations section 6; Production and planning section 6

    Procurement

    7 · Purchase Order tdpur4100m900 · stage 5 · real

    • Route — no menu entry; drill in from the purchase order list
    • Does — buy the components, and raise the inbound warehousing order on its own
    • Do - read the order the transfer named in its process report
    • Opens — Purchase to receipt · Create the purchase order, Book the lines

    Manufacturing

    9 · Production Orders tisfc0501m000 · stage 5 · real

    • Route — Manufacturing➔Job Shop➔Production Orders
    • Does — build the item: release, issue the components, report complete
    • Do - open the order the transfer created and release it
    • Opens — Plan to shipment · Build the pairs; Production order · Create the production order, Verify the generated foundation, Release the order, Issue material to the job shop, Report the operation complete and confirm warehouse receipt

    short-release · Components short at release · stage 5 · gate

    • Does — decide whether a production order releases while a component is short. Not documented for this release.
    • Setting — Check Shortages in Release Production Orders tisfc0204m000, Manufacturing➔Job Shop➔Production Control➔Release Production Orders

    Warehousing

    8 · Warehouse Receipt whinh3512m000 · stage 5 · step

    • Route — no menu entry; opens from Actions ➔ Receive on the inbound order
    • Does — book the bought components into stock
    • Do - enter the packing-slip reference per line and confirm
    • Opens — Purchase to receipt · Receive against the order, Confirm the receipt; Plan to shipment · Receive the components

    — · Inventory 360 whwmd4300m000 · stage 2 · read

    • Route — Warehousing➔Inventory 360
    • Does — answer the question the decision beside it asks. On-hand plus on-order for the item, which nothing in the sales order announces
    • Do - read on-hand at the shipping warehouse before the order is entered, and write the figure down
    • Walkthrough — Check an item's inventory
    • Leaves — nothing. It is a detour for information, and the only way to know which branch the route will take before it takes it
    • Opens — Check an item's inventory · Find the item, Read the stock by warehouse; Ship from stock · Confirm there is stock, Verify it worked; Plan to shipment · Preflight; Production order · Confirm the existing foundation; Purchase to receipt · Read the baseline, Verify the inventory increase; Warehouse transfer · Confirm stock, destination, and expected order type, Verify it worked

    stock · Finished item into stock · stage 5 · outcome

    • Does — hold the built item, which is only now sellable

    11 · Warehousing Order whinh2100m100 · stage 6 · step

    • Route — no menu entry; drill in from Warehouse Manager Dashboard whinh2300m000, Warehousing➔Manager Dashboard
    • Does — advise the outbound line, so there is stock to pick
    • Do - on the Outbound Lines toolbar, Actions ➔ Advice ➔ Generate Advice. Advised and Released both fill
    • Opens — Ship from stock · Generate outbound advice; Plan to shipment · Ship

    short-advice · Stock short at advice · stage 6 · gate

    • Does — decide whether outbound advice is generated when stock is short. Not documented for this release.
    • Setting — Create Outbound Advice Despite Inventory Shortage in Inventory Handling Parameters whinh0100m000, Warehousing➔Parameters➔Inventory Handling Parameters

    12 · Picking List whinh4525m100 · stage 6 · step

    • Route — Warehousing➔Outbound/Inspections➔Picking List
    • Does — confirm the advised quantity as picked. The line reaches Staged and a shipment is created
    • Do - tick the line, then Actions ➔ Pick Run
    • Opens — Ship from stock · Pick the goods; Plan to shipment · Ship

    13 · Shipment whinh4630m000 · stage 6 · terminal

    • Route — no menu entry; drill in from Shipments whinh4130m000, Warehousing➔Shipments➔Shipments
    • Does — freeze and confirm the shipment, which is where inventory leaves. On-hand drops by the shipped quantity
    • Do - Actions ➔ Freeze, then Actions ➔ Confirm. Confirming cannot be undone; a correction needs a return shipment
    • Opens — Ship from stock · Ship; Plan to shipment · Ship

    ship-short · Shipped less than picked · stage 6 · decision

    • Does — ship less than was picked; the rest becomes Not Shipped Quantity on the shipment line, and a backorder follows once the shipment is confirmed. Not documented for this release.
    • Setting — Confirm Back Orders automatically in Sales Order Parameters tdsls0100s400, a session in neither menu extract
    • Read — Shipment Lines whinh4131m000, no menu entry; drill in from Shipments whinh4130m000, Warehousing➔Shipments➔Shipments

    1. Plan to shipment — the process this shape belongs to; it walks the long route, task by task, and every claim about what a stage does is carried there.
